ordered_diagnoses: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma

s1.syndrome_frame: chronic pruritic eyelid plaque with lymphocytic infiltrates
salient_findings: pruritic, dark red plaque on the right upper eyelid
perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates around cystically dilated follicular infundibula
key_facts: 1-year history of a pruritic, dark red plaque on the right upper eyelid
plaque is 4 × 2-cm in size
plaque is erythematous, violaceous, indurated, and scaly with some papules
routine blood tests and biochemistry analysis were within normal limits
histopathologic examination revealed perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates
exocytosis of atypical lymphocytes into the epithelium
admixed plasma cells, eosinophils, and multinucleate giant cells
focal mild follicular mucin deposition on Alcian blue staining
lymphocytic infiltrates positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD7
lymphocytic infiltrates negative for CD8, CD20, CD30, CD79a, and CD56
CD4 to CD8 cells ratio within hair follicles > 7:1
monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement was demonstrated

shortlist: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathologic examination revealed perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates and monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement, consistent with mycosis fungoides

shortlist.label: Folliculotropic mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of a pruritic, dark red plaque on the eyelid and histopathologic findings of perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates and atypical lymphocytes are consistent with folliculotropic mycosis fungoides

shortlist.label: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Immunohistochemical analysis showed lymphocytic infiltrates positive for CD4 and a high CD4 to CD8 cells ratio, consistent with primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and histopathologic findings are consistent with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, although further specification is needed

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of a pruritic plaque and histopathologic findings of atypical lymphocytes and a mixed inflammatory infiltrate are consistent with lymphomatoid papulosis

raw.rationale: The presence of perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates, exocytosis of atypical lymphocytes into the epithelium, and focal mild follicular mucin deposition, along with a CD4 to CD8 cells ratio within hair follicles > 7:1 and monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement, are characteristic features of folliculotropic mycosis fungoides.

rejected.label: Mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: While mycosis fungoides shares some features, the specific follicular involvement and high CD4 to CD8 ratio point more towards the folliculotropic variant.

rejected.label: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histopathologic findings, including the presence of atypical lymphocytes and monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement, are more consistent with folliculotropic mycosis fungoides than a distinct CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes mycosis fungoides and its variants; the specific features of this case align more closely with folliculotropic mycosis fungoides.

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
rejected.why: The clinical and histopathological features, particularly the presence of a large, indurated plaque and the specific immunophenotypic profile, do not align with lymphomatoid papulosis, which typically presents with smaller, more transient lesions.
